Despite its limited natural resources, Liechtenstein is one of the few countries in the world with more registered companies than citizens; it has developed a prosperous, highly industrialized free-enterprise economy and a financial service sector as well as a living standard that compares favourably with those of the urban areas of Liechtenstein's much larger European neighbours.

Liechtenstein participates in a [customs union](/wiki/Customs_union "Customs union") with Switzerland and employs the [Swiss franc](/wiki/Swiss_franc "Swiss franc") as the national currency. In addition to developing the lift equation, the brothers also developed the equation for drag. It is of the same form as the lift equation, except the [coefficient of drag](/wiki/Coefficient_of_drag "Coefficient of drag") replaces the [coefficient of lift](/wiki/Lift_coefficient "Lift coefficient"), computing drag instead of lift. They used this equation to answer the question, "Is there enough power in the engine to produce a [thrust](/wiki/Thrust "Thrust") adequate to overcome the drag of the total frame ...", in the words of Combs. The Wrights then "... measured the pull in pounds on various parts of their aircraft, including the pull on each of the wings of the biplane in level position in known wind velocities ... They also devised a formula for [power-to-weight ratio](/wiki/Power-to-weight_ratio "Power-to-weight ratio") and propeller efficiency that would answer whether or not they could supply to the propellers the power necessary to deliver the thrust to maintain flight ... they even computed the thrust of their propellers to within 1 percent of the thrust actually delivered ..."[[73]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTECombs1979181–186,_367–375-74)

France have appeared in two of the eight [FIFA Confederations Cups](/wiki/FIFA_Confederations_Cup "FIFA Confederations Cup") contested and won the competition on both appearances. The team's two titles place in second place only trailing [Brazil](/wiki/Brazil_national_football_team "Brazil national football team") who have won four. France won their first Confederations Cup in [2001](/wiki/2001_FIFA_Confederations_Cup "2001 FIFA Confederations Cup") having appeared in the competition as a result of winning the FIFA World Cup in 1998. The team defeated [Japan](/wiki/Japan_national_football_team "Japan national football team") 1–0 in the final match. In the following Confederations Cup in [2003](/wiki/2003_FIFA_Confederations_Cup "2003 FIFA Confederations Cup"), France, appearing in the competition as the host country, won the competition beating [Cameroon](/wiki/Cameroon_national_football_team "Cameroon national football team") 1–0 after [extra time](/wiki/Extra_time "Extra time").

The upper reaches of the Yellow River constitute a segment starting from its source in the Bayan Har Mountains and ending at Hekou Town ([Togtoh County](/wiki/Togtoh_County "Togtoh County")), [Inner Mongolia](/wiki/Inner_Mongolia "Inner Mongolia") just before it turns sharply to the south. This segment has a total length of 3,472 kilometers (2,157 mi) and total basin area of 386,000 square kilometers (149,000 sq mi), 51.4% of the total basin area. Along this length, the elevation of the Yellow River drops 3,496 meters (11,470 ft), with an average [grade](/wiki/Grade_(slope) "Grade (slope)") of 0.10%.

The source section flows mainly through pastures, swamps, and knolls between the [Bayan Har Mountains](/wiki/Bayan_Har_Mountains "Bayan Har Mountains"), and the Anemaqen ([Amne Machin](/wiki/Amne_Machin "Amne Machin")) Mountains in Qinghai. The river water is clear and flows steadily. Crystal clear lakes are characteristic of this section. The two main lakes along this section are Lake Gyaring (Zhaling) and Lake Ngoring (Eling), with capacities of 4.7 billion and 10.8 billion m3 (166 and 381 billion ft3), respectively. At elevations over 4,290 m (14,070 ft) above sea level they are the two largest plateau freshwater lakes nationwide.
